note: Window agent p1820-p1829. US overshoot: the 'Louisiana' region (whole states) keeps Montana west of the Divide (Oregon Country) and Colorado/Wyoming west of the Adams-Onis meridian in the US shape; cut from the US keyframes of the window and given to Mexico. Loreto (Maynas) contested Peru/Gran Colombia 1825-1828.

region.text: Colorado and the strip of Wyoming south of 42N that lie west of 106 deg 20 min W, the meridian the Adams-Onis line follows north from the source of the Arkansas to 42N

events.note: The treaty line 'follows the southern bank of the Arkansas to its source' and, 'because the source lies south of 42N (about 39 deg 15 min N, 106 deg 20 min W), the line then runs due north along roughly the 106 deg 20 min W meridian to 42N, and west along 42N to the Pacific'; the treaty was 'officially made effective on February 22, 1821'. Ledger/37 of the same month gives back only the Cliopatria Mexico shape of 1846 inside four states (210 cells) and leaves about 330 cells of western Colorado and south-western Wyoming (the 'Louisiana' whole-state overshoot) in the US; this hands the rest to Spain, from which Mexico inherits it in September 1821.

region.text: Bessarabia between the Prut and the Dniester (modern Moldova), Russian since 1812

events.note: Ledger/71 (1828, occupation_start, counterpart ottoman-empire) names Moldavia and Wallachia, but its region also takes in Bessarabia, the Prut-Dniester half of Moldavia that Russia annexed in 1812 ('the Treaty of Bucharest (1812) ended the conflict, and the Ottoman Empire acknowledged the annexation', signed May 1812). The compiler therefore reads the 132 Bessarabian cells as Russian land occupied by the Ottoman Empire (roles reversed) from 1828 to the end of the window. This closes that reversed relation at once, so Bessarabia stays plain Russian land; the occupations of the principalities themselves belong to their own owners and are untouched.

Ledger/2 (1822, occupation_start, counterpart russian-empire) is read by the compiler as Circassia occupying Russian land: the 47 cells of Kabarda are drawn as Russian land hatched with Circassia's colour from 1822 to 1864. The page: Kabarda 'formally recognized Russian suzerainty' after 1779, 'most Kabardinian princes ultimately submitted to Russian rule' in 1809-1810, in 1820 it was 'declared property of the Russian government', and 'The area was placed under Russian military rule in 1822, as Kabardia eventually fully fell'. It is Russian land; this closes the reversed relation so the cells show as plain Russian land (the 1864 end of ledger/5 then closes nothing).

region.text: Maynas, the Amazon province of Loreto

events.note: Ledger/1 opens the contest over 'Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas' in 1822 and ledger/7 closes it in July 1829, but the keyframe republic-of-peru_1825 adds the 659 cells of Loreto afterwards as plain direct land, so the Maynas part of the contest is lost from 1825. The page: 'Jaen and Maynas' are 'the core of Gran Colombia's claims', which dated 'from colonial times', and only in the Armistice of Piura (10 July 1829) 'the Gran Colombia recognized Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas as Peruvian territories'. This re-marks Loreto as contested from 1826 (a keyframe snap comes after the year's events, so 1825 itself cannot carry it); it merges into the open contest and ends with ledger/7. The page does not say who held Maynas on the ground.

correction.text: the keyframe's own correction less the Oregon Country parts of Montana and Wyoming (west of the Continental Divide)

keyframe_overrides.why: The keyframe re-adds the 'Louisiana' whole-state overshoot: all of Montana, though the Oregon Country west of the Continental Divide was under joint occupation by the US and Britain from the Convention of 1818 until the Oregon Treaty of 1846. [Reviewer, 2 Nov: the Oregon Country cut was the gazetteer's 'Oregon Country' region, which in Montana runs to 112W and so also dropped about 168 cells of Missouri-basin land east of the Divide (Beaverhead, Glacier, the Rocky Mountain Front), Louisiana Purchase land, while its Wyoming part was empty; replaced by Montana west of the Continental Divide (284 cells) and Wyoming west of the Divide north of 42N (118 cells). The Oregon Country page: the region lay 'west of the Rocky Mountains' and 'east to the Continental Divide', took in 'parts of Montana and Wyoming', and the two countries 'agreed to "joint occupancy"' under the 1818 treaty until the Oregon Treaty of 1846 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Country).]
